scenario.summary: The threat actor UAT-12643 utilizes the Overlord RAT to retrieve encrypted command-and-control configurations from public blockchains including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana. By using JSON-RPC queries to public node providers like Infura and QuickNode, the malware resolves its C2 infrastructure through immutable ledger data such as Solana Memo transactions or Ethereum smart contracts.

meta.rationale: Start by identifying all hosts interacting with public blockchain RPC providers. Widen the search if initial results are concentrated in developer or research departments where such traffic is baseline.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using public blockchain ledgers as dead-drop resolvers for C2 configuration, identified by outbound RPC calls to node providers followed by rare network beaconing to resolved endpoints.

hunt.name: Decentralized Blockchain C2 Resolution
hunt.description: This hunt identifies attempts to resolve command-and-control infrastructure using Web3 nodes. It looks for DNS and HTTP traffic directed at public blockchain RPC providers that correlate with rare outbound network connections. By abusing immutable ledgers like Solana and Ethereum, attackers bypass traditional domain sinkholing. The hunt baselines typical developer RPC usage and highlights hosts that reach out to the blockchain and then initiate unique outbound sessions, often targeting non-standard ports within a narrow temporal window.

config.scoping_notes: Start by identifying all hosts interacting with public blockchain RPC providers. Widen the search if initial results are concentrated in developer or research departments where such traffic is baseline.
config.beyond_detection: A static rule for blockchain domains triggers too many false positives from developer activity. This hunt uses multi-surface correlation (DNS -> HTTP -> Network) and a temporal constraint to isolate the automated resolution-to-beaconing sequence.

nodes.label: DNS lookups to blockchain RPC nodes

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, pid, query_hostname, COUNT(*) AS lookup_count, MIN(time) AS first_lookup FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rpc_providers}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, pid, query_hostname
config.description: Identify hosts and processes resolving known blockchain RPC provider domains as a lead for potential dead-drop resolution.
config.expected_signal: Hosts and specific processes resolving blockchain domains. Legitimate developer activity will show high volume across multiple distinct providers; malicious resolution is typically low volume and tied to unusual processes.

primitive_config.label: DNS lookups to blockchain RPC nodes
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, pid, query_hostname, COUNT(*) AS lookup_count, MIN(time) AS first_lookup FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rpc_providers}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, pid, query_hostname
primitive_config.expected: Hosts and specific processes resolving blockchain domains. Legitimate developer activity will show high volume across multiple distinct providers; malicious resolution is typically low volume and tied to unusual processes.

nodes.label: HTTP POST activity to RPC endpoints

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_path, http_method, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rpc_providers}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND http_method = 'POST' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Focus on the HTTP POST requests that carry JSON-RPC payloads, which are required for querying specific blockchain data like transactions or logs.
config.expected_signal: POST requests to RPC providers from the scoping hosts. Analysts should look for unusual User-Agents or paths that do not match standard browser or developer tool patterns.

primitive_config.label: HTTP POST activity to RPC endpoints
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, url_hostname, url_path, http_method, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rpc_providers}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND http_method = 'POST' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: POST requests to RPC providers from the scoping hosts. Analysts should look for unusual User-Agents or paths that do not match standard browser or developer tool patterns.

nodes.label: Rare outbound connections from RPC hosts

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE direction = 'outbound' AND disposition = 'Allowed' AND (dst_endpoint_port NOT IN (80, 443, 53)) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Identify non-standard outbound connections occurring on hosts that have also performed blockchain RPC lookups, prioritizing non-standard ports.
config.expected_signal: A connection to a rare external IP address on a non-standard port. Correlation is strongest when this connection follows an RPC lookup by the same host.

primitive_config.label: Rare outbound connections from RPC hosts
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_network_connection WHERE direction = 'outbound' AND disposition = 'Allowed' AND (dst_endpoint_port NOT IN (80, 443, 53)) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, process_name HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
primitive_config.expected: A connection to a rare external IP address on a non-standard port. Correlation is strongest when this connection follows an RPC lookup by the same host.

config.objective: Determine if a host is resolving C2 coordinates via blockchain. Specifically look for rare outbound network connections that occur shortly after (within 5-10 minutes) the identified RPC activity on the same host. Evaluate if the processes involved in both steps are consistent or related.
config.description: Analyze the temporal and behavioural relationship between blockchain interaction and rare network egress.
config.expected_signal: A verdict of malicious when a host interacts with a blockchain RPC provider and then, within minutes, initiates a rare connection to a new IP address.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign citing the specific correlated RPC and beaconing rows.

config.question: The triage-rpc-behavior verdict is malicious for at least one host.
config.condition: The triage-rpc-behavior verdict is malicious for at least one host.
config.description: Direct the hunt based on the agent's correlation of blockchain resolution and beaconing behaviour.
Neutralize the threat and preserve the in-memory artifacts characteristic of Overlord RAT and similar blockchain-backed malware.
config.instructions: Isolate the host from the network. Capture a full memory dump before rebooting or shutting down to preserve in-memory decrypters and the resolved C2 coordinates.

config.description: Verify the agent's findings and investigate the origin of the malicious process.
config.instructions: Review the process tree for the processes identified in the RPC lookups and outbound connections. Inspect any available HTTP payload data for Base64 or hex-encoded C2 strings. Validate if the activity matches the Overlord RAT's Solana-based dead-drop pattern.

config.description: Record findings and update exclusions to reduce false positives for legitimate developer activity.
config.instructions: Document all confirmed malicious hosts and the resolved C2 IP addresses. If legitimate developer workstations were flagged, record their hostnames and typical RPC patterns for inclusion in the scope_hosts exclusion list for future runs.
